title: Standardize overload responses + Retry-After to improve client backoff during regional events
author: Peter Holtz
release_notes: API gateway now emits standardized overload responses with Retry-After to reduce retry storms during regional failover and capacity events.
Clients may observe more 429/503 responses (instead of timeouts) with explicit backoff guidance.
commits: gateway: add overload response helper + Retry-After header plumbing
gateway: distinguish capacity-shed vs hard-unavailable and map to 429/503 consistently
gateway: add retry-budget aware shed path to avoid amplifying thundering herd
docs: document overload semantics + client guidance (idempotency + streaming reconnect)
tests: integration tests for headers, status codes, and structured error payload
description:
Summary: During regional impairment/failover and capacity exhaustion, we currently manifest overload primarily as timeouts or inconsistent 5xx responses depending on which layer trips first (gateway timeout vs upstream rejection vs routing redirect). This tends to cause aggressive client retries and amplifies thundering herd at the worst time. This PR standardizes overload responses across the gateway so clients receive explicit backoff guidance via Retry-After, and we preserve consistent error shapes for observability and support.

Motivation / incident context: In staging rehearsals and the Q1 controlled failover prep work, we saw short spikes of 5xx and tail latency coincident with routing policy flips. A large portion was attributed to clients retrying quickly after gateway timeouts (no Retry-After) and some SDKs treating 503 differently from 429. We want deterministic, documented behavior to support graceful degradation instead of cascading overload.

What’s included: (1) Standard overload response helper (shared for all endpoints) that emits a consistent JSON error payload and sets Retry-After (seconds) for overload conditions; (2) Status code mapping: 429 for "shed / backpressure" (capacity pressure, retryable) and 503 for "temporarily unavailable" (hard-unavailable or upstream unavailable, retryable) with Retry-After; (3) Wiring into circuit breaker + upstream timeout paths so we return an explicit overload response before the request hits the global timeout when the retry budget is exhausted or the region is in a degraded state; (4) Streaming behavior: if we detect overload before first byte, return the standard overload response with Retry-After; if overload occurs after headers are sent, we send a structured terminal event (best-effort) and close, and the docs clarify client reconnect guidance; (5) Metrics: overload_response_total labeled by route + reason (bounded set), and retry_after_seconds histogram to support tuning.

Error payload (example): {"error": {"type": "overloaded", "message": "Service is temporarily overloaded. Please retry.", "retryable": true, "reason": "capacity_shed"}} plus header Retry-After: <seconds>. Note: this is intentionally aligned across chat/completions/embeddings/rerank so SDKs can implement one retry policy.

Retry-After computation: We derive Retry-After from the circuit breaker/open state + queue depth + retry budget state. Default is 2s with jitter (0–250ms). When in sustained shed mode, we increase up to 10s (capped) to dampen retry storms. We keep it conservative to avoid pushing clients into very long waits unless the system is clearly unhealthy.

Compatibility: This is not a breaking change in the sense of schema removal, but clients that were keying off specific 5xx codes may see more 429s during overload. Both are retryable. We document the guidance and ensure the error payload retains existing fields where present. For enterprise customers requesting auditability, this change improves the determinism of the user-visible symptom and makes it easier to correlate with failover events.

Testing: Added integration tests for each route ensuring: (a) overload path returns 429/503 as expected; (b) Retry-After exists and is within expected bounds; (c) error payload is consistent; (d) no accidental caching of overload responses; (e) streaming overload pre-first-byte returns a standard JSON response. Manual test notes included for staging with induced queue pressure.

Rollout plan: Guarded behind feature flag gateway.overload_retry_after_v1. Enabled in staging by default. In production, we will enable for a small percentage of Hosted traffic first (by tenant tier / allowlist) and watch: overload_response_total, overall 5xx rate, client retry amplification (request rate after overload), and p95/p99 latency. On-call runbook note: during regional failover tests, seeing 429/503 with Retry-After is expected and preferable to timeouts.

Follow-ups: This does not change SDK retry behavior directly (handled in SDK repos), but it unblocks predictable client backoff and better behavior during failovers. Also pairs well with ENG-2419 timeout/retry budget tuning and the streaming reconnect work.

Checklist: - [x] Added metrics (bounded labels) and updated cardinality review notes - [x] Updated docs for error semantics + client guidance - [x] Integration tests added for headers + payload - [x] Feature-flagged + default off in prod - [x] Alert annotations will be added in a separate PR when the controller emits failover events consistently

Notes for reviewers: Please pay special attention to (a) status code mapping choices (429 vs 503) and whether we should collapse to one; (b) streaming behavior after headers are sent; (c) label cardinality safety in overload_response_total.

---

CI: Buildkite (monorepo) ✅ build / unit ✅ lint ✅ integration ✅ gateway-e2e. One initial failure due to a flaky streaming integration test (timing); rerun passed after adding deterministic clock injection in the test harness.

Review conversation (highlights): Miles Thornton: "Can we ensure Retry-After is always present for the overload paths? Clients will do the wrong thing if it’s omitted." Author (Peter): "Yep, enforced in overload helper; added an assertion test for all overload responses." Mina Haddad: "Status code mapping: I like 429 for shed, but we should confirm we’re not violating any existing contract." Peter: "Agreed; updated docs and added release note. Also preserved existing error.type=overloaded." Ravi Menon: "Please ensure the reason labels are bounded; we can’t afford unbounded reason strings." Peter: "Changed reason to enum (capacity_shed | upstream_unavailable | retry_budget_exhausted | regional_degraded)." Allison Grant: "Add histogram for retry-after to help tune; also need a panel for overload vs timeout." Peter: "Added retry_after_seconds histogram; dashboard update will land in observability-pack." Tomáš Novák: "Runbook should mention that timeouts dropping while 429/503 rises is expected during a controlled failover." Peter: "Added note to docs/operator guide; runbook refresh tracked under ENG-2423."

Merge: Squash merged to main after approvals. Feature flag remains off in production by default; staged enablement planned during next game day rehearsal window.
